Below is the complete 12‑week programme (weeks 1–12) summarized week‑by‑week and session‑by‑session. It integrates the strength plan (three gym sessions/week), two cardio sessions/week, the core (abs) progression, Phase 2 increased pressing intensity, the Week‑12 1RM testing protocol, anti‑inflammatory nutrition guidance, and the sleep & recovery protocol. All exercises and progressions respect the physio instruction: avoid heavy axial spinal loading and loaded spinal flexion. Trap-bar deadlifts and seated/chest‑supported variations are prioritized. Read the notes and red flags at the end before implementing.

Quick orientation
- Frequency: 3 strength sessions/week (A, B, C). Add 2 cardio sessions/week (Cardio 1 = LISS, Cardio 2 = MIIT/tempo/intervals).
- Core: targeted core work added to each strength session (10–20 min depending on phase).
- Progression: 3 phases of 4 weeks: Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4) foundation; Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) strength with increased pressing intensity; Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12) strength/power and Week 12 testing/deload.
- RPE guidance: start conservative RPE 5–7 in Phase 1; Phase 2 main lifts push RPE 7.5–8.5; Phase 3 include some heavier sets (RPE 8–9) but Week 12 is a deload with a targeted 1RM testing day midweek.
- Rest: 2–3 min between main heavy sets; 60–90s for accessory work; 2.5–3 min for heavy presses in Phase 2.
- Safety: avoid weighted spinal flexion, heavy back squats, conventional deadlift with poor hinge. If pain/neurology appears, stop and refer to physio.

Equipment assumed available: trap/hex bar (preferred), kettlebells, dumbbells, cable machine, bench (incline), machine presses/rows, bands, TRX, bike/rower/elliptical, foam roller.

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Foundation (movement quality, posterior chain control)
Goal: teach hinge, thoracic mobility, unilateral control, anti‑flexion core. Moderate loads, technique focus.

Weekly schedule example (Mon/Wed/Fri strength; Tue/Sat cardio)
- Mon: Strength A (Lower + Core)
- Tue: Cardio 1 (LISS)
- Wed: Strength B (Upper push/pull + Core)
- Thu: Optional active recovery (walk/mobility)
- Fri: Strength C (Single‑leg/stability + Core)
- Sat: Cardio 2 (MIIT/tempo)
- Sun: Rest/active recovery

Weeks 1–4 — Session details

Session A — Lower + Core (approx 55–70 min)
Warm-up 10–12 min: 5 min bike/row, thoracic rotations, PVC hip hinge 2×10, glute bridge 2×10
Main:
1) Trap-bar deadlift (light-moderate): 3 × 6–8 (RPE 5–7)
2) Goblet squat: 3 × 8–10
3) Split‑stance RDL (DB or bodyweight): 3 × 8 each leg
4) Step-ups (DB light): 3 × 8 each leg
5) Pallof press (band/cable): 3 × 10–12 each side
Core:
6) Forearm plank: 3 × 30–45s
Cool-down: hamstring/hip flexor stretches, breathing

Session B — Upper push/pull + posterior chain (55–65 min)
Warm-up 8–10 min: 5 min row, band pull‑aparts, shoulder T‑spine mobilization
Main:
1) Incline dumbbell press: 3 × 8–10
2) Seated chest‑supported cable row: 3 × 8–10
3) Single‑arm dumbbell row (bench supported): 3 × 8 each arm
4) Face pulls: 3 × 12–15
5) Suitcase carry: 3 × 40–60 m each side
Core:
6) Bird-dog: 3 × 8–10 each side (3s hold)
Cool-down: pec stretch, scapular mobility

Session C — Mobility + single‑leg focus (55–65 min)
Warm-up 8–10 min: bike/elliptical, hip/ankle mobility
Main:
1) Bulgarian split squat (BW → DB): 3 × 8 each leg
2) KB Romanian deadlift: 3 × 8–10
3) Cable/band anti‑flexion chop: 3 × 10 each side
4) TRX/ring rows: 3 × 8–12
5) Farmer carry bilateral: 3 × 40–60 m
Core:
6) Dead‑bug: 3 × 8–10 each side
Optional finisher: 6–10 min steady-state cardio

Cardio — Phase 1
- Cardio 1 (LISS): 25–30 min bike/brisk walk, RPE 4–5.
- Cardio 2 (MIIT tempo): ~20–25 min intervals: e.g., 6 × 1.5 min moderate (RPE 6–7) + 1.5 min easy.

- Dead-bug, bird-dog, Pallof, planks as above. 2–3 short sessions/week (10–12 min).

- Protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day; calories adjusted to goal (maintenance ± 200–300 kcal).

The plan avoids heavy axial spinal loading and loaded spinal flexion (no heavy back squats, heavy deadlifts, or bent-over loaded flexion). It focuses on progressive, safe strength, improving posterior chain control, core stability, hip hinge patterning with low spinal load, and general conditioning. Assume client cleared by physio for controlled resistance work and has basic familiarity with gym equipment. If any new pain or neurological symptoms occur, stop and refer to physio/MD.

Overview and structure
- Duration: 12 weeks divided into 3 phases (each 4 weeks).
- Frequency: 3 gym sessions/week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri). Optional light mobility/walk/cardio on off days.
- Each gym session ~55–75 minutes including warm-up and cool-down.
- Progression: increase load, reps, or complexity each week within phases; switch emphasis each phase.
- Load guidance: start conservative (RPE 6–7 of 10). Avoid heavy axial compression > moderate loads. Use goblet/suitcase/kettlebell work, trap bar or hex bar for deadlift variations if available (prefer trap bar modified neutral posture), Romanian deadlifts with light–moderate weight and emphasis on hip hinge/form, cable machines, single-leg work, and anti‑flexion core work.
- Core rule: no loaded spinal flexion (no weighted sit-ups, heavy bent-over rows that cause flexion under load). Rows are okay if neutral spine supported.
- Warm-up: 8–12 minutes dynamic mobility and activation (detailed below).
- Recovery & lifestyle: guidance at end.

Phase 1 — Foundation, movement quality, and load tolerance (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: rebuild movement patterns, restore thoracic mobility and hip hinge mechanics, improve trunk control and unilateral strength. Keep loads moderate; prioritize neuromuscular control.

Weekly split (3 sessions/week): A, B, C (rotate)

Session A — Lower-body + Core emphasis
Warm-up (10–12 min)
- 5 min bike/row easy
- Thoracic rotations (standing or on foam roller) 8–10/side
- Hip hinge drills: PVC dowel hip hinge 2×10, then light kettlebell deadlift patterning 2×8

Main work

2) Goblet squat (kettlebell/dumbbell): 3 × 8–10. Keep torso upright; range pain-free.
3) Split stance RDL (bodyweight->light dumbbell): 3 × 8 each leg. Emphasize hip hinge, balance.
4) Step-ups (bench or 12–16” box) holding dumbbells light: 3 × 8 each leg.
5) Pallof press (anti-rotation) with cable/band: 3 × 10–12 each side.
6) Plank (forearm) — time control: 3 × 30–45s, neutral spine.

Cool-down (5–8 min): hamstring and hip flexor stretches, deep breathing.

Session B — Upper-body horizontal/press + posterior chain
Warm-up (10 min)
- 5 min row easy
- Shoulder T-spine mobilizations, band pull-aparts 2×15

Main work
1) Incline dumbbell press: 3 × 8–10.
2) Seated cable row (chest-supported if available): 3 × 8–10. Support minimizes lumbar load.
3) Single-arm dumbbell row with bench support: 3 × 8 each arm.
4) Face pulls: 3 × 12–15.
5) Suitcase carry (dumbbell at side) 3 × 40–60m each side — core anti-lateral-flexion.
6) Bird-dog (slow, controlled) 3 × 8–10 each side.

Session C — Mobility, single-leg, conditioning
Warm-up (10 min)

Phase 2 — Strength and unilateral load (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: increase strength while still protecting spine; add more unilateral work and heavier but controlled loads; introduce trap-bar heavier sets if tolerated; add more core anti-extension/anti-rotation challenges.

Warm-up similar with hinge drills and breathing.

3) Single-leg RDL (dumbbell): 3 × 8 each leg, heavier than Phase 1.

- Weeks 5–8: increase load and complexity; introduce heavier trap-bar deadlifts and unilateral load. Aim for 4–5 sets on main lifts. Continue no loaded flexion.
- Weeks 9–11: heavier, lower-rep strength emphasis with power elements (kettlebell swings), higher conditioning. Monitor tolerance. Week 12: deload (reduce volume 30–50%, keep light technique work).

- Stop and refer if new or returning radicular symptoms (shooting pain, numbness, tingling into legs), progressive neurological deficits, or increasing low-back pain during or after sessions.

- Modality options: stationary bike, brisk treadmill walk (incline optional), elliptical, pool swim.
- Duration: start 25–35 minutes in Phase 1, progress to 35–45 minutes in later phases.

1) Dead-bug (anti-flexion, classic starter)
- How: Lie on back, hips & knees 90/90. Brace core, lower one leg and opposite arm slowly while keeping lumbar spine in neutral (no gap increase). Return.
- Progression: increase ROM of leg extension, add light band resistance, slow tempo.
- Sets/reps: 3 × 8–12 reps per side.

2) Bird-dog (anti-extension/anti-rotation)
- How: From hands & knees, brace and extend opposite arm & leg keeping hips square and spine neutral. Avoid sagging or rotating pelvis.
- Progression: slow tempo holds, add short holds (3–6 s), or perform from elevated surface (bench) to increase difficulty.
- Sets/reps: 3 × 8–10 per side, hold 3–6s.

3) Pallof press (anti-rotation)
- How: Cable or band at chest height. Step sideways, brace, press the handle straight out and hold briefly resisting rotation, then return.
- Progression: increase band tension, offset foot stance, add slow eccentric.
- Sets/reps: 3 × 10–15 seconds hold or 8–12 reps each side.

4) Half-kneeling anti-rotation (band or cable)
- How: Kneeling on one knee, core braced, press/pull cable across body resisting rotation.
- Progression: taller posture, weight on front knee, longer hold.
- Sets/reps: 3 × 8–12 each side.

5) Farmer carry & suitcase carry (anti-lateral flexion & anti-rotation)
- How: Walk 30–60 m carrying weights — keep torso tall and braced.
- Progression: heavier loads, longer carries, uneven carry transitions.
- Sets/reps: 3 rounds of 30–60 m each (can be done as part of strength sessions).

6) Plank variations (isometric anti-flexion)
- Forearm plank, high plank, single-leg plank, or plank with scapular protraction/retraction.
- Progression: increase hold time, add arm/leg lifts, do RKC/ab band resisted plank for higher intensity.
- Sets/reps: 3 × 30–60 s depending on level. Start at shorter durations and build.

7) Stir-the-pot (advanced anti-flexion)
- How: Forearms on Swiss ball, plank position, move arms in small circles while maintaining neutral spine.
- Progression: reduce circle size or time under tension; ensure no lumbar sag.
- Sets/reps: 3 × 20–30s.

8) Anti-extension rollouts (knee or incline) — controlled, low-load
- How: From knees with ab wheel or hands on Swiss ball, perform small rollouts only as far as core can maintain neutral spine.
- Contra: avoid deep full rollouts if client cannot maintain neutral lumbar control.
- Sets/reps: 3 × 6–10 (knee rollouts) keeping range small initially.

9) Lateral work: side plank and side bridge variations
- How: Side plank on elbow or hand, knees bent regression if needed.
- Progression: full leg, add hip dips, weighted side plank holds.
- Sets/reps: 3 × 20–45s each side.

10) Controlled Pallof press anti‑rotation chops and lifts (dynamic anti-rotation)
- How: From cable/band, perform slow “chop” or “lift” patterns focusing on trunk control and hip movement rather than spinal flexion.
- Sets/reps: 3 × 8–12 each direction.

11) Glute‑focused core: dead bug variations combined with glute bridge

- Sets/reps: 3 × 8–12 marches per side.

- Be cautious with heavy barbell rollouts, high-volume crunches, or excessive repeated spinal flexion/extension.

All exercises and progressions respect the physio instruction: avoid heavy axial spinal loading and loaded spinal flexion. Trap-bar deadlifts and seated/chest‑supported variations are prioritized. Read the notes and red flags at the end before implementing.

Quick orientation
- Frequency: 3 strength sessions/week (A, B, C). Add 2 cardio sessions/week (Cardio 1 = LISS, Cardio 2 = MIIT/tempo/intervals).
- Core: targeted core work added to each strength session (10–20 min depending on phase).
- Progression: 3 phases of 4 weeks: Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4) foundation; Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) strength with increased pressing intensity; Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12) strength/power and Week 12 testing/deload.

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Foundation (movement quality, posterior chain control)
Goal: teach hinge, thoracic mobility, unilateral control, anti‑flexion core. Moderate loads, technique focus.

- Mon: Strength A (Lower + Core)
- Tue: Cardio 1 (LISS)

4) Face pulls: 3 × 12–15

6) Bird-dog: 3 × 8–10 each side (3s hold)

4) TRX/ring rows: 3 × 8–12
5) Farmer carry bilateral: 3 × 40–60 m

Cardio — Phase 1

- Only test lifts he’s trained with good form (pref: trap-bar deadlift and incline or seated press).

- Weeks 1–4: Dead-bug, bird-dog, Pallof, planks (motor control).
- Weeks 5–8: Pallof progressions, farmer carries, side planks, single‑leg RDL with pause (capacity).
